raw_response:
*Speaking in first person as the farmer*

Aiya, let me think through this year. I'm getting old — 71 now — but I've been working these fields for 50 years, so I know what they need. My son lives in the city, so it's just me and my husband at home. Twelve mu isn't much, but for two old people it's already a lot of work.

Let me think about how to split the land. I'll do wheat-maize double crop on 8 mu — that's our main grain, feeds us and the extra we sell. Then 4 mu cotton on the sandy piece by the road. I've thought about giving up cotton because the picking is killing my back, but the price has been decent and I can get my niece to help in October for a few days pay.

**Wheat (already planted last October, harvesting in June):**
I put down about 20 kg of compound fertilizer as base before sowing, plus some manure from the neighbor's chickens. Then I'll topdress maybe 10 kg of urea at jointing in March — if the wheat looks yellow I'll add more, if it looks strong I'll hold back. The extension guy last year said 15 kg N per mu is enough but I usually do a bit more because I don't want a thin crop. I irrigate three times: once in winter if it's dry, once at jointing, once at heading. If spring rain is good I skip the heading one to save money. I bought a semi-improved variety last year from the shop, paid around 35 yuan per mu for seed. I expect around 420 kg per mu — last year was 440 but the year before only 380 because of that late frost. My neighbor Wang got 480 but he has better land.

**Maize (planting mid-June right after wheat):**
Very tight turnaround — I hire the custom tractor to come the same day we finish wheat harvest, it costs but I can't do it by hand at my age. Plant hybrid seed, the Zhengdan variety everyone around here uses, about 45 yuan per mu. Fertilizer about 15 kg N per mu, most at planting, topdress once at knee-high stage. I only irrigate once or twice — maize is tougher than wheat about water, and summer usually has rain. Expect 480 kg per mu. The maize does well here most years.

**Cotton (planting late April):**
This is the worry crop. I plant 4 mu on the sandy piece. Cotton likes the sun, doesn't want too much water. I use maybe 13 kg N per mu, split across base and bud stage. Cotton pests — the bollworm especially — means I have to spray 3 or 4 times, that's the biggest cost after labor. Irrigate twice, once after planting and once in August during boll-setting. The picking is the hard part — I pick what I can, hire help for about 10 days, pay around 80 yuan a day. Last year I got 240 kg lint per mu, hoping for similar. Cotton prices have been OK so I'll keep doing it one more year.

**Overall:** Total I'll spend maybe 3,200 yuan on inputs this year. I keep some cash back for emergencies — at my age I don't take chances. If fertilizer prices jump I'll cut back a bit on the wheat topdress, not the base.
